sentences.text:
: 
G.A. 
 Court No. - 12
 Hon'Ble Pankaj Bhatia, J. 
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Aga and perused the record.

2. The accused-applicant seeks bail in FIR/Case Crime No.10 of 2018 under sections 376-D, 452,
506 Ipc, P.S. Risiya, District Bahraich.

3. The Fir in question was lodged through an application under section 156(3) Cr.P.C. alleging the
commission of rape on 15.11.2017.

4. Submission of the counsel for the applicant is that the Fir was lodged at the instance of the wife
of the applicant against the son of the informant through an application under section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
and as a sequel to the same, the present Fir has been lodged.

5.  Considering the fact that the victim has even refused to undergo medical examination aged about 45 years at the time of lodging the FIR and there being no material to corroborate the allegations, prima-facie a case for bail is made out more so when the applicant has no criminal history and is in jail since 26.08.2025.
Thus the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Sahaj Ram be released on bail in aforesaid FIR/Case Crime Number subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- (Twenty Thousand) each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(Pankaj Bhatia,J.) October 8, 2025 VNP/-
 
Sahaj Ram vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
